comment: QEMU configure arguments of the SGI release build. A key such as windows-arm64 adds to its operating system's list on that architecture; Clang 23 in MSYS2's CLANGARM64 environment turns warnings in QEMU's own code (util/rcu.c, an unused global) into errors that -Werror would stop the build on. sgi-package.py builds the archives with them and scripts/ci/sgi-check compiles the Windows programs with the same list, so a flag edit is compiled on every pull request. The Linux archive builds with Debian 12's GCC 12, which warns (maybe-uninitialized, in hw/coproc/dsp56300/dsp56300-ops.c) where the pull-request compilers do not, and a release must not stop on a compiler's warnings, and the CHD library's C++ runtime is linked statically so the archive does not need the host's libstdc++. The Windows prefix, bindir and suffix make QEMU find its data in share/qemu beside bin/, as it does on Linux and macOS; its default prefix, c:/, defeats the relocation, and the data search then looks in c:/share. sgi-package.py adds --static to the Windows build, which the cross-check leaves out because the Fedora image has only shared MinGW libraries. The disabled features keep the archive from depending on what else a build machine has installed. Every archive links the same static GnuTLS from vcpkg, which supplies QEMU's ciphers (VNC password authentication, LUKS images) and its TLS (VNC, NBD, migration), so no crypto or TLS library comes from the build machine. QEMU takes its ciphers from GnuTLS, so libgcrypt and nettle stay off; nettle in particular is the 4.x vcpkg carries, whose nettle_gcm_digest takes five arguments where QEMU's own nettle backend passes six. The rust list applies to the platforms sgi-package.py names in RUST_PLATFORMS; scripts/ci/sgi-check leaves it out because its Fedora cross image has no cargo or clang.
